# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

# Repository Exploration Report: /app

## 1. Codebase Structure

**Language/Framework:** Python 3.9 + Flask (1.1.2), served by gunicorn on port 9898 (see `/app/Dockerfile`). Heavy use of **pandas** (`np.select` over vectorized regex conditions), plus `fuzzywuzzy`/`python-Levenshtein` for name matching (`/app/categorizationapp/setup.py`).

**Purpose:** An Indian bank transaction enrichment service ("transaction-enrichment-python" per Dockerfile). Rule/regex-based categorization of bank statement narrations for ~37 Indian banks.

**Layout:**
```
/app
├── Dockerfile, .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap (port 9898)
        ├── Controller.py               # 936 lines: HTTP endpoints, per-bank dispatch
        ├── BankScripts/                # 37 per-bank categorizers (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared logic: purpose, clean names, PFM, salary, internal pay
```

**Entry points (`Controller.py`):**
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py:69-936`. Huge if/elif ladder per bank (`ANDHRA_BANK` at :91, `SBI` :115, `ICICI` :139, `HDFC` :163, ... `PAYTM_BANK` :715, `STANDARD_CHARTERED` :739, etc.). Pipeline per bank: `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` → `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (CC only) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` → optional `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`.
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — `Controller.py:55-67`.

## 2. Categorization & Payee-Name Extraction Logic

### Core assignment mechanism
Every bank script builds a list of `[boolean-mask, label]` pairs evaluated with `np.select` — **first matching rule wins**; default category is `"TRANSFER"`. Each script sets, in order: `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, then `partyName` (payee extraction), then several cleanup passes.

### Per-bank categorizers (transactionCategory: cheque/transfer/NACH/refund/reversal/mandate)
All in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/`. Representative example — **HDFC.py** (`categorize_HDFC_transactions`, lines 9-277):
- Mandate/account verification (penny drop): line 13
- Refund: lines 19-20; Card payment reversal: line 21; UPI/IMPS/ATM reversals: lines 22-24; generic REVERSAL: line 25
- ECS/NACH penalty: line 26; auto-payment (ACH/SI/NACH debit): lines 27, 51; auto-credit (`^ACH C`): line 55
- Cheque: return penalty :30, cash withdrawal :50, CHEQUE_RETURN :69-72, CHEQUE_PAID :71/74, CHEQUE_DEPOSIT :73/75/100
- Transfer rails: TPT :57, UPI :58, IMPS :59, NEFT :60, RTGS :61, FUND_TRANSFER :96
- Heuristic reversal/bounce via adjacent equal-amount debit→credit pair: lines 98-99
- **Payee extraction (partyName)**: lines 141-273 — token-splitting via `sep_by_dash`/`sep_by_colon` and regex `py_extract` (e.g., UPI :154, IMPS/NEFT :155-163, POS via `HDFC_POS_PATTERN` :164, ACH/NACH debit :169-174, cheque via `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1-10` :188-197, transfers via `HDFC_FT_PATTERN*` :200-215), followed by cleanup passes :223-273.

Other notable per-bank hotspots (same structure):
- `BankScripts/SBI.py` — ECS_PENALTY :29, AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES :33, AUTO_CREDIT (`ACHCr|NACH00`) :48, AUTO_PAYMENT (`CMP MANDATE|ACHDr`) :49; name extraction uses `SBI_AUTOPAY1-9`, `SBI_INB_*`, `SBI_CP_*` patterns.
- `BankScripts/Kotak.py` (327 lines) — NACH tax-refund :12, mandate charges :39, AUTO_CREDIT/AUTO_PAYMENT :44-45, NACH salary :89; extensive NACH party extraction :124-135; ECS prefix/suffix cleanup :276-301.
- `BankScripts/ICICI.py` — verification :11, NACH bounce (`REV_NACH`) :18, mandate charges :32, ECS penalty :42.
- `BankScripts/PNB.py` — mandate charges :14, ECS penalty :32, AUTO_PAYMENT (`^NACH-DR|^ECS/`) :37, AUTO_CREDIT :40, NACH name extraction :142-143, cheque payee via `PNB_CHQ_0-8`.
- `BankScripts/StandardCharted.py` — NACH debit return :24, ACH bounce charges :36, NACH DR/CR :59-61, NACH payee extraction :119-122.
- `BankScripts/Axis.py` — mandate-based ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION :24-26; `BankScripts/Indusind.py` — mandate verification at amount==2 :30.
- `BankScripts/IDFC.py`, `IDBI.py`, `UnionBank.py`, `UCO.py`, `YES.py`, `KarurVyasa.py`, `Karnataka.py`, `SouthIndian.py`, etc. — all have analogous NACH/ECS/cheque/reversal/refund blocks (see grep hits above, e.g. `UnionBank.py:18,24,30,40-41,78-79`; `KarurVyasa.py:22-37,89-103`; `YES.py:19,80`).

### Shared regex constants
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (432 lines) — per-bank patterns: account-verification (`ACC_VERIF` :6, `BANK_VER_ICICI` :69, `BANK_VER` :327), SBI autopay/mandate (`SBI_AUTOPAY1-9` :33-41), HDFC cheque (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1-10` :81-90), fund-transfer (`FT_PATTERN*`, `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1-37` :241-299), ECS penalty (`ECS_PENAL` :111, `ECS_PENAL_YES` :387), reversal (`REVERSAL_KV` :344, `REVERSAL_YES` :394, `REVERSAL_CITY` :349), refunds (`REFUND_KV` :339, `REFUND_UCO` :373, `VISA_REFUND_PATTERN` :182), cheque cleanup (`CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` :318, `CHQ_CLEAN`/`CHQ_CLEAN2` :361-362).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` (191 lines) — semantic/purpose patterns: `SALARY` :6, `LOAN*` :9-18, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` :86, `INSUFF_BOUNCE` :87, `REFUND` :91, `TAX_REFUND` :103, `INTERNAL_PAY` :93, plus merchant taxonomies (SHOPPING, UTILITY, INSURANCE, ...).

### Downstream shared enrichment (UtilityScripts/)
- **`Purpose.py`** — `purpose(transactions, accountType)` :9-300. Assigns `transactionSubcategory` (LOAN :23-25, RENT_INCOME :140, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE / INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE for cheque returns :145-147, TAX_REFUND :156, REFUND :158) and blanks names for charges/reversals :173, :294.
- **`CleanName.py`** — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` :9-1971. The master payee-normalization file: maps raw `partyName`/`description` fragments to canonical merchant names (DTH :13-26, broadband :29-50, electricity :53-..., NACH loan issuers e.g. `NACH- DR/EQUITAS` :602, `^NACH-DR/HDFC BANK LIMITED/0` :1747, `^NACH- DR/INDUSIND` :1756), suffix normalization (Pvt Ltd :1909-1916), and sets `merchantType` :1948-1956 and subcategory overrides :1958-1967.
- **`CardCleanNames.py`** (928 lines, `card_clean_names` :9) and **`CardPurpose.py`** (`card_purpose` :9; refund/reversal exclusions :16, :38) — credit-card equivalents.
- **`InternalPayment.py`** — `internal_payment()` :8-62; fuzzy-matches `partyName` vs account holder (`fuzz.ratio` > 75) to flag `INTERNAL_PAYMENT`; excludes `CHEQUE_RETURN`/`REVERSAL` :16, :31, :49.
- **`SalaryDetection.py`** — `salary_detection()` :16; excludes REVERSAL/RETURN/REFUND categories :46, :98, :151.
- **`PFMCategorization.py`** — `pfm_categorization()` :8-206; rolls categories up to PFM buckets (REVERSAL rollup :73, TRANSFER rollup :74, TAX_REFUND :180).
- **`SimpleDescription.py`** :6-19; **`RecurrentTxns.py`** :8-25.
- **`AppUtil.py`** — the extraction primitives used everywhere: `sep_by_` (split on `/`) :14, `sep_by_dash` :17, `sep_by_colon` :29, other separators :20-45, `fuzzy_match` :48, `py_extract` (regex `str.extract` with NaN handling) :61-66, `clean_input_df` :6.
- **Enums (labels only, not enforced in code):** `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` :3-171 (CHEQUE_COLLECTION :9, TAX_REFUND :11, ATM_REVERSAL :12, NACH :37, CHEQUE_RETURN :44, AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES :84, CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL :94, UPI_REVERSAL :99, ECS_BOUNCE :167) and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` :3-136 (REFUND :14, CHEQUE_BOUNCE :36, ECS_BOUNCE :59, REVERSAL :76).

## 3. Test Files

**None exist.** No `test*/*test*` files anywhere in the repo (globs for `**/*test*` and `**/*Test*` return nothing); no pytest/unittest configuration; `setup.py` declares no test dependencies. The only test-related artifact is a `.gitignore` entry for `TEST*.xml` (unit test reports), suggesting tests existed upstream but were not imported.

## 4. Git History

```
fc21c7f import codebase   (the only commit)
```

- **Single commit** `fc21c7f73731ab3aa5bfa41f48bfbccd64fa8abf`, author `t <t@t>`, dated Wed Jul 15 02:30:30 2026, "import codebase" — imports all 54 files (11,242 insertions).
- Only branch: `main`. No other branches, no stashes, reflog contains only the initial commit, and the working tree is **clean** (no uncommitted modifications).
- Therefore **no diffs of "recent changes" exist** — the entire codebase was squash-imported in one commit, and any prior change history (including changes to the categorization code) was discarded at import time. If you're hunting a regression, you cannot bisect within this repo; you'd need the upstream repository history.

### Practical debugging pointers
Given no test coverage and no history, the highest-risk areas for categorization bugs are:
1. **Rule ordering** — `np.select` is first-match-wins; e.g. in `HDFC.py` the generic REVERSAL rule (:25) fires before ECS_PENALTY (:26) and cheque rules (:69-75), and broad regexes like `ver` inside `ACC_VERIF` (`BankRegexConstants.py:6`) can over-match.
2. **Adjacent-row heuristics** using `.shift(periods=1)` (e.g. `HDFC.py:98-99`, `StandardCharted.py:60`, `HDFC.py:126`) — sensitive to transaction sort order in the request payload.
3. **Token-index extraction** (`sep_by_dash(desc, n1, n2)`) — silently returns empty/wrong tokens when narration formats drift.
4. Amount-based mandate/verification rules (`amount.eq(1)`, `amount.eq(2)`, `amount.lt(2)`) in nearly every bank script, including the aggressive `Axis.py:26` (any credit of exactly 1 → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION) and `Indusind.py:31` (any debit of 1).

steps.message:
All five reported failures are fixed with four one-line rule corrections (no restructuring). Each fix targets a dead or off-by-one condition, so nothing that matched correctly before can change.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. Cheque filed as generic transfer** — `Indusind.py:64`
The remark-only cheque rule matched exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`), but standard cheque numbers are 6 digits, so a note containing just the cheque number fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. Widened to `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (the same convention Axis.py:58-59 already uses), so 5-digit remarks keep their current label and 6-digit cheque numbers are rescued.

**2. Salary payee shows "NACH"** — `IDBI.py:83`
`ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` splits on `-` into `[ACH, BD, NACH, ACME INDUSTRIES]`; the rule took token 2 (`NACH`) instead of token 3. Fixed to `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)`. The sibling rule for `^ACH-BD-` (no `NACH`) at line 84 correctly keeps 2,3 and is untouched.

**3. Blank sender name on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`-style rows** — `IDBI.py:110`
The extraction pattern `"[0-9]{10,} (.*)"` has a single capture group (index 0), but `py_extract` was called with `index=1`; `py_extract` returns an empty series when the group index doesn't exist, blanking the name. Fixed to `index=0` (every other single-group `py_extract` call in the codebase uses 0).

**4. Mandate token confirmation filed as transfer** — `Axis.py:25`
The rule only fired for amount exactly 1, so the ₹2 token confirmation debit flagged `MANDATE` fell to the default `TRANSFER`. Changed to `amount.isin([1,2])` — ₹1 mandates keep their current `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` label, ₹2 is rescued (matching the mirrored Indusind rule at line 30 which recognizes ₹2 mandates).

**5. Card refund labeled `REFUND` instead of `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, varying by account category** — `Indusind.py:26`
The rule compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`, but the controller only ever passes `SAVING`, `CURRENT`, or `CREDIT_CARD` — the condition was dead, so savings customers fell to the next rule and got plain `REFUND`. Fixed the typo to `"SAVING"`; POS credits ≥ 10 on savings accounts now read `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, while sub-₹10 credits still fall to `REFUND` and `CURRENT`-account behavior (`CARD_RECEIPTS` path) is unchanged.

## Verification
Reproduced all five tickets against the buggy code, then re-ran after the fixes — all five now label/name correctly. Control rows in the same runs (ordinary UPI/NEFT purchases and transfers, plain `ACH-BD-<name>` credits, 5-digit cheque remarks, tiny POS credits, ₹1 mandates, `NACH-DR` auto-debits, CURRENT-account POS receipts) are byte-for-byte unchanged, and an end-to-end run through the full Controller pipeline (`purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment` → `salary_detection`) confirms the downstream passes preserve the corrected labels.
